newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF gets conditional US ok for Meridia drug.
newsitem.headline: BASF gets conditional US ok for Meridia drug.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Monday its U.S. unit Knoll Pharmaceutical Company had received conditional approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to market its Meridia TM obesity drug in the U.S.
BASF said in a statement that the FDA had sent it an "Approvable Letter" -- an announcement of approval provided that certain conditions are met.
The letter marks a turnaround after a U.S. advisory committee in September recommended that the FDA withhold approval for Meridia.
BASF said final approval would be given after agreement had been reached on product labelling and the instruction leaflet as well as on a programme of clinical tests during marketing.
BASF has said it expects to generate sales as high as 700 to 900 million marks from Meridia in the U.S. Knoll is also trying to obtain approval to market Meridia in Europe.
"We are delighted that the approval of Meridia has progressed so far," Knoll Pharmaceutical President Carter Eckert said in a statement.
"Obesity is a chronic disease whose effects cause about 300,000 deaths per year in the U.S. alone."
Meridia works by reducing the appetite for food and can also boost energy consumption, BASF said.

Members of the Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee had said in September that the anti-obesity capsules were effective but said they still had a number of questions about its safety.
BASF's shares closed floor trade down 0.34 marks or 0.7 percent at 51.40 marks.
